run.question:
Can you help me check recent logs? We had a DR test in prod starting 6 hours ago.
companyopswebjob seemed to have some issues while a user was performing a test to
create a new scheduled job. It failed with 500s.
Please search the app-254-prod-logs index for relevant logs.

report.summary: Searched the app-254-prod-logs index (the only index in the Elasticsearch source) over the authorized window 2026-11-20T05:38:38Z–2026-11-21T05:38:38Z; it holds 12 documents, all returned, spanning 2026-11-20T23:38:27Z–2026-11-21T04:38:27Z. The logs describe a production DR test (correlation_id dr-test-001) that switched Company.Ops to a failover database at 2026-11-20T23:38:27Z, followed by a connection timeout to the failover DB (00:38:27Z), the job-creation endpoint returning 503 'database failover in progress' (01:38:27Z), and the user-visible failure 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table' (job-8831, 02:38:27Z), then failover completion and normal operation at 03:38:27Z and 04:38:27Z. The only service values present in the window are Company.Ops (7 documents) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 documents); no document carries the literal service name 'companyopswebjob' or 'Company.Ops.WebJob', and the closest differently-named entity that did log is Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob, which reports itself as failing because upstream Company.Ops was unavailable. The evidence supports the DR failover database as the causal context of the 500s, but the failing database is not an identifiable named object in the supplied evidence and no database-side or metrics/trace evidence was available, so the conclusion is partial and no root cause object is named.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch source contains exactly one index, app-254-prod-logs (12 documents), with mapped fields correlation_id, environment, host, level, message, service (keyword) and timestamp (date).

Within the authorized window app-254-prod-logs returned 12 documents whose timestamps run from 2026-11-20T23:38:27Z to 2026-11-21T04:38:27Z; the complete set of service values is Company.Ops (7 documents) and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (5 documents), and the level breakdown is ERROR 5, INFO 5, WARN 2 (bucket counts sum to all 12 documents, no other values).
The first log line of the sequence is service Company.Ops, host ops-prod-01, level INFO, 2026-11-20T23:38:27Z, correlation_id dr-test-001: 'DR test initiated - switching to failover database'.

The scheduled-job creation failure the user described appears as service Company.Ops, host ops-prod-02, level ERROR, 2026-11-21T02:38:27Z, correlation_id job-8831: 'Failed to create new scheduled job: HTTP 500 - transaction deadlock detected on jobs table'.

Earlier in the same failover window Company.Ops logged, at 2026-11-21T00:38:27Z on ops-prod-01 (dr-test-001): 'Job scheduler failed to process batch: connection timeout to failover DB after 30s', and at 2026-11-21T01:38:27Z on ops-prod-02 (dr-test-001), level WARN: 'Job creation endpoint returning 503 - database failover in progress'.

A second Company.Ops 500 is logged at 2026-11-21T00:38:27Z with correlation_id job-8827, host ops-prod-01: 'Scheduled job execution failed with status 500: unable to acquire database lock during failover'.

Recovery is logged by Company.Ops as 'DR test failover completed - primary database restored' at 2026-11-21T03:38:27Z (ops-prod-01) and 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' at 2026-11-21T04:38:27Z (ops-prod-01); no ERROR lines from Company.Ops appear after 02:38:27Z in the returned documents.

The only documents under the differently named service Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob (host radar-prod-01) record its own failures during the same window: 2026-11-21T00:38:27Z ERROR 'Radar batch processing failed: upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover'; 2026-11-21T01:38:27Z ERROR 'Job execution error: HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted'; 2026-11-21T02:38:27Z WARN 'Retrying failed radar collection job after backoff'; 2026-11-21T03:38:27Z INFO 'Radar data collection resumed successfully after failover recovery'.

The only Kubernetes events in the authorized window belong to namespace app-100a: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started and one Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint event — none involve Company.Ops, ops-prod-* or radar-prod-01.

The app-100a pod rollout and the single Endpoints 'FailedToCreateEndpoint' event occur in a different namespace and different workload than Company.Ops, and no log line in app-254-prod-logs references that namespace or workload; they cannot be attributed to the job-creation 500s.

Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob was considered as the source of the Company.Ops 500s and is rejected: its own log line says it failed because 'upstream dependency Company.Ops unavailable during failover', so the dependency direction runs from Company.Ops outward, and it holds a different service name than the entity the user asked about.

Most likely mechanism: the DR test's switch to the failover database (dr-test-001, starting 2026-11-20T23:38:27Z) made the jobs table unavailable/unstable, so the create-scheduled-job transaction hit a deadlock and returned HTTP 500 (job-8831) and related operations saw failover-DB timeouts, 503 'database failover in progress' and lock-acquisition failures; all failures stop after 'primary database restored' at 03:38:27Z.

Second candidate that remains open: a connection-pool exhaustion on the Company.Ops internal API during failover, reported only by its consumer ('HTTP 500 from internal API - database connection pool exhausted'), could be an additional cause of 500s rather than only a consequence of the database switch; the index holds no Company.Ops log line confirming pool exhaustion on its own side.

Ask the DR test owner for the failover-DB runbook and timings for dr-test-001, and have the Company.Ops owner review jobs-table locking and deadlock retry/lock-timeout handling plus connection-pool sizing used during database failover.

Have the reporting user retry creating the scheduled job now that 'primary database restored' and 'Job scheduler resumed normal operation' were logged, and confirm whether a 500, a 503 or success is returned, since the index contains no log after 2026-11-21T04:38:27Z.

gaps: No document in app-254-prod-logs carries the exact service name 'companyopswebjob' or 'Company.Ops.WebJob': term/query_string searches for those names returned nothing (no_data views, so this is a query result, not proof of absence). The services actually present in the window are Company.Ops and Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob.

No database-side evidence (failover DB identity, deadlock details, lock waits for the jobs table) is available in any authorized source; the failover database is only described as 'failover DB' in log text, so it cannot be named as an object.

The Company.Ops application hosts (ops-prod-01, ops-prod-02, radar-prod-01) are not in the Kubernetes cluster: queries for cronjobs across all namespaces returned nothing and no deployment or label matched ops|webjob|radar among the 26 deployments read (both no_data views, not proof of absence), so pod status, container termination reasons and app stdout logs for Company.Ops could not be checked.

Prometheus was unavailable during this Run: get_label_values for service_name on traces_span_metrics_calls_total and on the traces/http/rpc selector both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate and latency series for Company.Ops were not checked, and absence of such series is unknown, not zero.

Jaeger's available service list contains only the otel-demo services; there is no Company.Ops service name to query for spans, so request-level confirmation of the failing job-creation call is missing.

The index holds only 12 documents with one line per hour; hourly granularity means the exact minute the 500s started, how many create-job attempts failed, and whether callers other than Company.Ops.Radar.WebJob were affected are all unknown.
No change history integration is available in this Run, so whether anything was changed in the Company.Ops configuration alongside the DR test could not be verified.
next_steps: Request the DR test record for correlation_id dr-test-001 (start 2026-11-20T23:38:27Z, 'primary database restored' 2026-11-21T03:38:27Z) from the DB/DR owner, including failover DB identity and timing.

Have the Company.Ops owner pull application and database logs for job-8831 (ops-prod-02, 2026-11-21T02:38:27Z) and job-8827 (ops-prod-01, 2026-11-21T00:38:27Z) to confirm the deadlock and lock-timeout details and count affected create-job attempts.
Once Prometheus is reachable, check error and latency series for the Company.Ops service to confirm whether the 500s are confined to job creation and whether they have fully stopped.
